definitions.ask: Should `.` also become `@` at an item or bullet-body start, such as on an empty draft?
definitions.why: Matches your example and the `=` alias rule, and keeps a whole-item `.` free

choices.label: Only a `.` after a space that follows task text becomes `@`; line starts stay literal
A `.` at an item or bullet start also becomes `@`; leading dotfiles and `.5` need `..`

definitions.ask: Should the `..` escape require the second `.` within 350 ms of the first?
definitions.why: You asked for "twice fast enough"; it reuses the `=` alias's 350 ms window and probe

choices.label: Only a fast second `.` escapes, like fast `==`; a slow one types after the `@`
The next `.` escapes at any speed, like `\` `\`; a slow `..` never leaves `@.`

definitions.ask: Should Space and Escape on the alias-opened, still-empty route list restore the literal `.`?
definitions.why: A bare `@` then a space is never a valid route, and it matches the `=` opener

choices.label: Space gives `. ` and Escape gives `.`, closing the list, like the `=` opener
Space types after the `@` and Escape only closes the list; only `..` and Undo restore
